criteria.criterion: crates/athena-context/prompts/reader.md tells the reader to check whether the outcome needs a change to athena.toml, defaults.toml or a file under .github/workflows/, and if so to list that file as a deliverable and name it in an acceptance criterion.
criteria.evidence: I read the diff. reader.md line 15 now says: "Check whether the outcome needs a change to athena.toml, defaults.toml, or a file under .github/workflows/; if it does, list that file as a deliverable and name it in an acceptance criterion."

criteria.criterion: crates/athena-context/prompts/producer.md tells the producer that when it finds it needs a governance file the reading does not list, it stops and reports it instead of editing the file.
criteria.evidence: I read the diff. producer.md adds: "If you need a governance file (athena.toml, defaults.toml, a workflow, tool or lint configuration) that the reading does not list as a deliverable, stop and report it in open_issues; do not edit it." This is in the shared frame, so it covers every capability.

criteria.criterion: A new test in crates/athena-context/src/lib.rs checks that the reader frame carries the governance-check wording, names .github/workflows/, and that the producer frame carries the stop-and-report wording. Run `cargo test -p athena-context`.
criteria.evidence: The new test reader_checks_for_governance_files_and_producer_stops_on_unlisted_ones checks the reader wording, ".github/workflows/" and the list-and-name phrase, plus the producer's stop-and-report phrase. 29 tests passed, including this one.

criteria.criterion: A new test shows that a reading for a workflow change (for example a deliverable of .github/workflows/ci.yml) is accepted by governance_change_is_listed only when the workflow is listed as a deliverable and named in a criterion, and that is_governance recognizes the workflow path. Run `cargo test -p athena-core governance`.
criteria.evidence: The new test a_workflow_change_must_be_listed_and_named in admission.rs checks: is_governance(".github/workflows/ci.yml") is true; a reading with neither the listing nor the naming is refused; listed but not named is refused; listed and named is accepted; named but not listed is refused. It passes when run by name. The cited filter `governance` does not select it, though: that run executed only governance_files_are_recognized (1 test). See finding.

criteria.criterion: The reader and producer frames still fit their token budgets and the whole workspace passes: run `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check`.
criteria.evidence: Every test binary reported ok with 0 failed, including the athena-context budget tests (the_contract_is_within_its_budget, producer_and_verifier_frames_leave_room_for_capability_sections). Clippy finished clean and fmt --check printed nothing.

criteria.criterion: No governance file (athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows, Cargo lints) is modified by this change.
criteria.evidence: The diff touches only CHANGELOG.md, the two prompt files, athena-context/src/lib.rs and athena-core/src/admission.rs. None of these is a governance file.

findings.summary: The cited command for criterion 4 does not run the new workflow test
findings.evidence: `cargo test -p athena-core governance` ran 1 test (governance_files_are_recognized) and filtered out 162. The new test's name does not contain "governance", so the criterion's own command never runs it. Run by name, it passes. Renaming it, e.g. to a_workflow_governance_change_must_be_listed_and_named, would fix this.

findings.summary: The reader's governance list got less specific
findings.evidence: "the [lints] tables of Cargo.toml" became just "[lints] tables", which no longer says which file. "CI workflows" was dropped from the general list; it now appears only in the new check sentence as .github/workflows/. The rule is still covered, but the file named for [lints] was lost.

findings.summary: Other prompt lines were reworded for brevity
findings.evidence: Several unrelated lines were shortened without changing their meaning, most likely to stay within the token budgets. This is not in the request but is harmless.

summary: The change does what was asked. The reader prompt now has an explicit step to check whether the outcome needs athena.toml, defaults.toml or a file under .github/workflows/, and if so to list that file as a deliverable and name it in an acceptance criterion. The producer prompt now says to stop and report, not edit, a governance file the reading does not list. New tests check the prompt wording and that a reading for a .github/workflows/ci.yml change is accepted only when that file is both listed and named. All five changed files are on the deliverables list, and no governance file was touched. I ran `cargo test -p athena-context`, `cargo test --locked`, clippy and fmt in this snapshot, and all passed. One minor problem: the command criterion 4 cites, `cargo test -p athena-core governance`, does not select the new workflow test because its name lacks \"governance\". The test passes when run by name. The reader prompt also got slightly less specific about [lints] tables (it no longer names Cargo.toml).
